lines: Scott Ramsower, who runs private equity funds at the $250 billion Teacher Retirement System of Texas, argues continuation vehicles are inherently conflicted because the GP is both seller and buyer, so every deal needs bespoke scrutiny of pricing, process and alignment.

He warns CVs and NAV loans can produce 'synthetic' DPI that flatters track records, and that routinely moving top assets into CVs strips commingled funds of the right-tail upside that drives PE returns.
He sees a growing pile of 'zombie funds' that can neither exit assets nor raise new capital, which will absorb LP governance time and drag on industry performance.

Ramsower argues semi-liquid retail PE products undermine the asset class's core edge, since illiquidity protects long-term value creation, and that fee-paying CVs cannibalize the fee-free co-investment flow LPs built over decades.
His answer is 'craftsmanship alpha': pairing quantitative diligence with a qualitative read of GP partnership cohesion that tends to crack when performance slips.
podcast: Capital Allocators – Inside the Institutional Investment Industry
title: Continuation Vehicles from the LP Seat – Scott Ramsower (EP.523)
